fullCitation: Eldjarn GH, et al. Large-scale plasma proteomics comparisons through genetics and disease associations. Nature. 2023.
sampleSize: 54,219 UKB-PPP (Olink) vs ~36,000 Icelanders (SomaScan); 1,514 measured on both
keyFindings: Compared Olink Explore 3072 in UK Biobank against SomaScan v4 in Iceland, the largest head-to-head proteogenomic comparison to date
Olink demonstrated stronger cis-pQTL enrichment (~72%) compared to SomaScan (~43%)
Poor cross-platform correlation for overlapping protein targets
63% of SomaScan pQTL associations involved variants associated with >10 proteins vs 52% for Olink; 28% of SomaScan proteins with any pQTL had only such non-specific associations vs 8% on Olink
Platform-specific disease associations highlight complementary utility

fullCitation: Katz DH, et al. Whole genome sequence analysis of protein measurement in the Jackson Heart Study and HERITAGE family study. Science Advances. 2022.
keyFindings: Head-to-head comparison of Olink vs SomaScan in two community cohorts
Modest cross-platform correlation for shared targets
Both platforms identify unique disease-relevant signals
Genetic instrument concordance varies substantially by protein

fullCitation: Kirsher D, Ahadi S, et al. Benchmarking eight commercial high-plex proteomics assays on a common set of plasma samples. Communications Chemistry. 2025.
keyFindings: Most comprehensive head-to-head comparison across 8 commercial platforms
SomaScan achieved best precision (median CV ~5.3%)
Olink Explore HT median CV ~26.8%; Seer ~26.4%; Biognosys ~29.8%
Cross-platform correlation remains poor for most protein targets
Platform choice should be driven by study-specific priorities

Supplementary Data 8 (MS-HAP Depletion arm) provides the Atlas's Biognosys TrueDiscovery protein list, 3,575 proteins by primary UniProt accession, a matched-cohort depletion-workflow list used from v2.8 in place of the earlier PQ500 spectral-library list

fullCitation: Rooney MR, et al. Comparison of proteomic measurements across platforms in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study. Clinical Chemistry. 2023.
keyFindings: Large-scale epidemiological comparison in ARIC
SomaScan v4 vs Olink Proseek head-to-head on same samples
Disease prediction performance varies by outcome and platform
Complementary rather than redundant information from each platform

fullCitation: Rooney MR, et al. Comparison of SomaScan 11K and Olink Explore HT in the ARIC study. medRxiv/Clinical Chemistry. 2024.
keyFindings: Updated comparison with SomaScan 11K and Olink Explore HT
Expanded plex worsens cross-platform agreement
SomaScan 11K shows more off-target aptamer binding at higher plex
Both platforms improve disease prediction over clinical models alone

fullCitation: Thrush KA, Haslam DE, et al. Stability and reproducibility comparison of Olink and SomaScan in the Nurses' Health Study. Proteomics. 2022.
keyFindings: Focused comparison of analytical stability and reproducibility
Both platforms show acceptable technical reproducibility
Olink shows better stability across sample handling conditions
SomaScan more sensitive to pre-analytical variation

fullCitation: Pietzner M, et al. Three-platform proteomics in the Genes & Health cohort. medRxiv. 2025.
keyFindings: First large-scale 3-platform comparison including Seer Proteograph
Seer detected up to 8,067 protein groups via MS-DIA
MS-based approach particularly strong for non-European ancestry populations
Seer uniquely detects protein-altering variants and resolves epitope effects
Complementary platform insights for diverse population proteomics

fullCitation: Alamar Biosciences. NULISA: a proteomic liquid biopsy platform with attomolar sensitivity and absolute quantification. Nature Communications. 2023.
keyFindings: Demonstrated attomolar-level sensitivity (0.1 pg/mL)
Dual-capture and release mechanism reduces background noise
Strong performance for Alzheimer's disease biomarkers (p-tau217, Aβ42/40)
APOE genotyping achievable from same protein panel

fullCitation: Nomic Bio. nELISA: a miniaturized, bead-based sandwich immunoassay for high-plex absolute protein quantification. Nature Methods. 2025.
keyFindings: First demonstration of absolute quantification at 1,000-plex
Pre-colocalized antibody pairs achieve 99.99% specificity
Throughput exceeds 1,000 samples/day
Cost structure enables population-scale studies at ~$50/sample
Measurements span 8 orders of magnitude dynamic range

fullCitation: Sissala N, Babačić H, Leo IR, et al. Comparative evaluation of Olink Explore 3072 and mass spectrometry with peptide fractionation for plasma proteomics. Communications Chemistry. 2025;8:327.
sampleSize: 88 plasma samples (lung cancer cohort, KUH Stockholm)
keyFindings: Largest MS–Olink head-to-head to date by overlapping proteins (n=1,129 shared)
Median cross-platform Spearman correlation ρ=0.59 (IQR 0.33–0.75); rises to ρ=0.68 on high-quality subset
Platforms exhibit complementary coverage: Olink stronger at low-abundance targets; MS stronger at mid-to-high abundance
Tier 1 pQTL proteins (Eldjarn confidence tiers) showed higher MS–Olink agreement (ρ=0.71 vs ρ=0.50 for tier 3)
MS–Olink correlations were consistently higher than Olink–SomaScan correlations for matched proteins
Note: MS method is HiRIEF LC-MS/MS (DDA, TMT-labelled), not Seer Proteograph XT; Olink panel is Explore 3072, not HT

fullCitation: PRECISE-SG100K Consortium. Multi-platform proteomics in 100,000 Southeast Asian participants. Preprint. 2025.
keyFindings: Largest multi-ancestry proteomics study to date
Three-platform comparison in Southeast Asian populations
Population-specific protein associations identified
Cross-platform concordance varies by ancestry and protein class
